title: HYPOChLorous Acid TEsting Studies: Elective Groin VASCULAR Surgery
summary:
This study investigates whether standardized irrigation of the surgical wound during vascular surgery procedures in the groin can reduce the risk of postoperative wound infections.

At Heidelberg University Hospital, two groups of patients will be compared: patients who underwent surgery before the introduction of the new clinical standard and therefore did not receive antiseptic wound irrigation, and patients who undergo surgery after the introduction of this standard. In the latter group, the surgical wound is irrigated with a hypochlorous acid–containing solution (Granudacyn®) before wound closure. If synthetic vascular graft material is implanted, it is additionally rinsed with the solution prior to implantation.

The main outcome assessed is the occurrence of surgical wound infections after surgery. Additional outcomes include other postoperative complications, length of hospital stay, and the use of antibiotic therapy.

The analysis is based on routinely collected clinical data from the electronic patient record.
